newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japanese firms see rise in interim profits.
newsitem.headline: Big Japanese firms see rise in interim profits.

text.p: First-half profits announced by large Japanese firms showed an average increase of 10 percent from the year-ago period, a corporate survey showed on Monday.
Wako Research Institute of Economics said it based its figures on interim parent current profit results announced by 292 companies.
It said the average gain in the firms' parent current profits in the six months to September 30 over the year-ago period was 10.41 percent.
Current profit is pre-tax profit which includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
Wako tracks 766 large companies, of which 292 have announced half-year results so far in the current earnings period.
All 766 firms are listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and have business years ending on March 31. The list does not include banks, brokerages or insurance firms.
The after-tax parent interim profits of the 292 firms surged 13.31 percent against the previous year, while parent sales were up 4.91 percent, the research arm of Wako Securities Co said.
